[Skip to main content](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#content) [Skip To search](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#search-box) [Skip To Alex Virtual Assistant](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#alex-virtual-assistant) # T4 Zone or overseas forces 2026 Complete question T4 in your supplementary tax return if you can claim a zone or overseas forces tax offset. **Last updated** 30 May 2026 Print or Download ## On this page - [Things you need to know](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#ato-Thingsyouneedtoknow) - [Completing your supplementary tax return](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#ato-Completingyoursupplementarytaxreturn) - [Where to go next](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#ato-Wheretogonext) ## Things you need to know You may be able to claim this tax offset if you: - lived in a specified remote or isolated area of Australia (not including an offshore oil or gas rig) - served in a specified locality overseas as a member of the Australian Defence Force or a United Nations armed force. If you qualify for both an overseas forces tax offset and a zone tax offset, you can claim only one of them. Claim the one that gives you the higher tax offset. ### Zone tax offset We base your eligibility for the [zone tax offset](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/tax-offsets/zone-or-overseas-forces-tax-offsets/zone-tax-offset) on your usual place of residence. If your usual place of residence wasn't in a zone, you're not eligible for the zone tax offset. Remote areas are specified as either Zone A or Zone B. There are also locations that are particularly isolated within zones, known as special areas. If you don't know which zone your area is in, see [Australian zone list](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/tax-offsets-australian-zones#ato-Zonetaxoffset). #### Example: residence not in a remote area Michael is a maintenance engineer contractor who lived in Brisbane during the 2025–26 income year (not a specified zone). He flew to Blackall in Queensland (a Zone B location) where he worked in the mining industry. As Michael's usual place of residence wasn't in a zone, he isn't eligible for the zone tax offset. End of example #### Example: residence in a remote area Louise lived in Darwin (a Zone A location) during the 2025–26 income year. She travelled to Kununurra in Western Australia (a Zone A location and special area) for her job in the mining industry. Louise drove to Kununurra, completed a 14-day shift at the mine, and then drove back to Darwin at the end of her working shift, where she remained for 16 days. As Louise's usual place of residence was Darwin (Zone A location), she is eligible for the zone tax offset for Zone A. End of example To qualify for the tax offset, your usual place of residence must have been in a remote area (not necessarily continuously), for either: - 183 days or more during 2025–26 - 183 days or more during the period 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2026 (including at least one day in 2025–26) and you were unable to claim a zone tax offset in your 2024–25 tax return. If your usual place of residence is in a zone for less than 183 days in 2025–26, you may still be able to claim a tax offset as long as your usual place of residence is in a zone for a continuous period of less than 5 years after 1 July 2020 and both of the following apply: - you're unable to claim in the first year because you lived there less than 183 days - the total of the days you lived there in the first year and in 2025–26 is 183 or more (the period you live in a zone in 2025–26 must include **1 July 2025**, the first day of the income year). #### Example: remote area for a continuous period of less than 5 years Garry lived in a remote area from 1 March 2021 to 30 September 2025, a continuous period of less than 5 years. He couldn’t claim a zone tax offset for the first year because he was living there for only 122 days. However, he could carry forward these unused days to 2025–26. He now adds the number of days from 1 March 2021 to 30 June 2021 (122 days) and the number of days from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2025 (92 days). As the total (214 days) is ‘183 days or more’ over those 2 income years, Garry can claim the tax offset in his supplementary tax return 2025–26. End of example ### Overseas forces tax offset You may be eligible for an overseas forces tax offset if you served in a specified overseas locality as a member of the Australian Defence Force or a United Nations armed force in 2025–26 and income relating to that service isn't specifically exempt from tax. Periods of service for which your income was ‘exempt foreign employment income’ are excluded in working out your eligibility for the tax offset. Your employer will be able to advise you whether you served in a locality that qualifies for the overseas forces tax offset. You can also see which localities qualify for the overseas forces tax offset at [Specified overseas localities](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/tax-offsets/zone-or-overseas-forces-tax-offsets/overseas-forces-tax-offset#ato-Specifiedoverseaslocalities). To claim the full tax offset, you must have served in the overseas locality for 183 days or more in 2025–26. If your overseas service was less than 183 days, you may be able to claim part of the tax offset. Unlike the zone tax offset, you can't carry forward any unused days from previous years to make up 183 days. If you served in an overseas locality for less than 183 days, you may still be entitled to claim the full overseas forces tax offset if the total of the following is 183 days or more: - the total number of days you served in the overseas locality - _plus_ the number of days you served in one or more zones. If you served as a member of the Australian Defence Force, days spent in a zone must be defence force service. If you don't live in a zone or serve in an overseas force, go to question [T5 Invalid and invalid carer 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t5-invalid-and-invalid-carer-2026). ## Completing your supplementary tax return The zone or overseas forces tax offset is made up of: - a fixed amount - a base amount. The **fixed amount** is a prescribed amount available to all people in the zone or overseas area eligible for the tax offset. You may be able to include a **base amount** if you either: - maintained a child under 21 or full-time student under 25 - were entitled to claim the [Invalid and invalid carer tax offset](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/invalid-and-invalid-carer-tax-offset-calculator). Your fixed and base amounts are determined by your circumstances. ### How to work out your tax offset – simple circumstances Follow the steps to work out your tax offset. #### Step 1 Your tax offset is the amount in [table 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table1), if: - your usual place of residence was in only one zone or you served in only one specified overseas locality for at least 183 days - you're not able to include a base amount as - you weren't entitled to claim the invalid and invalid carer tax offset - you either didn't have a dependent child or student at any time in 2025–26, or if you did have a dependent child or student, their adjusted taxable income (ATI) was equal to or greater than $282 _plus_ $4.12 for each day you maintained them. | Zone A | Zone B | Special
area | Overseas
forces | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $338 | $57 | $1,173 | $338 | Table 1: Tax offset amounts Child includes your adopted child, stepchild, ex-nuptial child and child of your spouse. A student must be full-time at a school, college or university. If your circumstances are more complex, you can't use [table 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table1). See, [How to work out your tax offset – more complex circumstances](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Howtoworkoutyourtaxoffsetmorecomplexcirc). If you received a remote area allowance from Centrelink or the Department of Veterans’ Affairs, you must reduce the amount of your zone tax offset by the amount of allowance you received. #### Step 2 Write your tax offset amount less any remote area allowance at question **T4 Zone or overseas forces** – label **R** in your supplementary tax return. Don't show cents. Go to, [Where to go next](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Wheretogonext29). ### How to work out your tax offset – more complex circumstances If your circumstances are more complex, work out your base amount, if any, using either: - [Zone or overseas forces tax offset calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/income-tests-calculator) - [Working out your total base amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Workingoutyourtotalbaseamount). ### Dependent child or student base amount Work out your base amount for a dependent child or student. #### Full-year claim Your base amount will include the maximum amount in [table 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table2) for each student under 25 years old on 30 June 2026 in full-time education at a school, college or university, and for each child under 21 years on 30 June 2026 who, for the whole of 2025–26: - is treated as an Australian resident - is maintained by only you, and - has an ATI of less than $286. To calculate the ATI see [Adjusted taxable income for you and your dependants 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2026-instructions/supporting-information-individual-tax-return-2026/adjusted-taxable-income-for-you-and-your-dependants-2026) or use the [Income tests calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/income-tests-calculator). If you don't have any dependent children or students, go to [Invalid and invalid carer base amount](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Invalidandinvalidcarerbaseamount). | Dependant | Base amount | | --- | --- | | Each student under 25 years old | $376 | | For the oldest non-student child under 21 years old | $376 | | Other non-student children under 21 years old | $282 for each child | Table 2: Dependant child or student base amount For the meaning of dependant, see [Tax time definitions](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/tax-time-definitions#D). If all of these requirements were met, add up the base amount for each child or student and write the total at [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **a**. If 2 or more people contributed to the maintenance of a dependent child or student, each person can only claim a proportion of the base amount. If the requirements were met for only part of the year, or your child’s or student’s ATI for the period you're claiming this base amount in respect of them was $286 or more, you may be able to claim for a part of the base amount. Read on. #### Part-year claim You can claim only part of the base amount for dependent children or students if any of the following apply: - the child or student was an Australian tax resident for only part of 2025–26 - the student was under 25 years old and in full-time education for only part of 2025–26 - the child or student was maintained by you for only part of 2025–26 - the child turned 21 years old during the year and was not in full-time education for the remainder of the year - the student was 25 years old at 30 June 2026. Use **worksheet 1** to work out the reduced base amount for each eligible dependent child or student as described in [table 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table2). | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Maximum base amount for the child or student from [table 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table2). | $ | | b | Number of days you maintained your child or student and your child or student was an eligible dependant. | days | | c | Number of days in 2025–26. | 365 | | d | Divide row **b** by row **c**. | $ | | e | Multiply row **d** by row **a**. | $ | Worksheet 1 – Reduced base amount for eligible dependent child or student If the ATI of your child or student was less than $286 for the period you're claiming this base amount in respect of them, transfer amount at row **e** above to [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **b**. If you had more than one eligible child or student and the ATI of each one is less than $286 for the period you're claiming this base amount in respect of them, work out the amount for each child and student, add up all the amounts and write the total at [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **b**. ### If ATI was $286 or more for the period you maintained them You can't claim any base amount for your child or student if that child or student had an ATI equal to or greater than either: - the total of $282 _plus_ $4.12 for each day you maintained them for a student under 25 years old or for the oldest child under 21 years old who wasn't a student - the total of $282 _plus_ $3.09 for each day you maintained them for any other child under 21 years old who isn't a student. If your child’s or student’s ATI for the period you're claiming this base amount in respect of them was $286 or more but less than the limits shown, use [worksheet 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet2) to work out the base amount. | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Base amount for the child or student from [table 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table2) or [worksheet 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet1) – row **e** for a part-year claim. | $ | | b | Your child’s or student’s ATI for the period you maintained them. | $ | | c | Income above which the base amount begins to reduce. | $282 | | d | Subtract row **c** from row **b**. | $ | | e | Divide row **d** by 4 because your base amount is reduced by $1 for every $4 of ATI over $282. Don't show cents. | $ | | f | Subtract row **e** from row **a**. Show 0 (zero) if the amount is negative. Don't show cents. | $ | Worksheet 2 – Base amount where ATI exceeds $282 Transfer the amount at row **f** above to [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **c**. If you had more than one eligible child or student, work out the amount for each child or student, add up all the amounts and write the total at [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **c**. ### Sole parent base amount If you had sole care of a dependent child or student **and** you wrote an amount of at least $1 in [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) at rows **a**, **b** or **c** (base amount for dependent children or students), you may also be eligible for a sole parent base amount. You can only claim this base amount if you were a sole parent at any time during 2025–26, and either: - your usual place of residence was in a remote area of Australia - you served overseas as a member of the Australian Defence Force. Sole care means that you alone had full responsibility on a day-to-day basis for the upbringing, welfare and maintenance of a child or student. We don't consider you to have had sole care if you were living with a spouse (married or de facto) during the income year unless special circumstances exist. You will need to use [worksheet 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet3) to calculate a part-year sole parent base amount claim. #### Special circumstances If you had a spouse (married or de facto) at any time during 2025–26, you're entitled to a sole parent base amount only in special circumstances. Generally, for special circumstances to exist, you must have been financially responsible for and had sole care of the dependent child or student, without the support a spouse normally provides. Examples of situations where special circumstances may arise: - You were married at any time during 2025–26 but - during 2025–26, you then separated from, or were deserted by, your spouse, and - for the remainder of 2025–26, you weren't in a de facto relationship. - Your spouse was in prison for a sentence of at least 12 months. - Your spouse was medically certified as being permanently mentally incapable of taking part in caring for your child or student. If you're unsure whether special circumstances apply, [contact us](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us). ### Shared or joint custody after a relationship breakdown There are times, after a relationship breakdown, such as a divorce or separation, where both parents share the custody of a child or student. If you can show that you had sole care of a dependent child or student for part of the year, you may be able to claim the base amount for that part of the year. This means more than just having access visits with the child or student. We consider you to have sole care of the child or student for the part of the year up to the day the child turns 21 years old, or the student turns 25 years old if the dependant either: - isn't receiving full-time education and turns 21 years old during 2025–26 - is a full-time student and turns 25 years old during 2025–26. You're only entitled to claim the base amount for that part of the year before the birthday. If you had sole care of a dependent child or student for the whole of 2025–26, write **$1,607** at [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **d otherwise work out your part year claim using worksheet 3**. | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Number of days you had sole care of a dependent child or student | days | | b | Multiply row **a** by $4.40 | $ | Worksheet 3 – Sole parent base amount, part-year claim Transfer the amount at row **b** above to [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **e**. ### Invalid and invalid carer base amount If you're entitled to a tax offset at question **T5** – label **B**, you're entitled to this base amount. To work out the base amount you're entitled to claim, you can either: - use our [Invalid and invalid carer tax offset calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/invalid-and-invalid-carer-tax-offset-calculator) - go to question [T5 Invalid and invalid carer 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t5-invalid-and-invalid-carer-2026) to work it out manually. Then write the amount you work out above at [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **f**. ### Working out your total base amount Use **worksheet 4** to work out your total base amount. | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Dependent children or students, from [table 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table2) | $ | | b | Dependent children or students, from [worksheet 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet1) | $ | | c | Dependent children or students, from [worksheet 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet2) | $ | | d | Sole parent – full year | $ | | e | Sole parent – part year from [worksheet 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet3) | $ | | f | Amount claimed at question **T5** – label **B** | $ | | g | Add up all of these amounts | $ | Worksheet 4 – Total base amount The amount at row **g** is your total base amount. Read on. You use the information from **table 3** below when you complete either [worksheet 5](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet5) or [worksheet 6](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet6). | Zone or area | Fixed amount | Percentage of base amount | | --- | --- | --- | | Zone A | $338 | 50% | | Zone B | $57 | 20% | | Special area | $1,173 | 50% | | Overseas forces | $338 | 50% | Table 3: Zone fixed amount and percentage of base amount #### Final calculation Use the following information to work out the final calculation for the zone or overseas forces tax offset. Your usual place of residence was only in one zone or you served only in specified overseas localities for at least 183 days, go to [Category 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Category1). ### Multiple locations Check [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3), if both of the following apply: - your usual place of residence was in more than one zone or special area, or you served in specified overseas localities - you were in one of them for 183 days or more. If the fixed amount for that zone is higher than for the other zones where you were, use that fixed amount and [worksheet 5](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet5) to work out your tax offset. This will give you the greatest benefit. Otherwise, go to [Category 2](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Category2). #### Example: using a fixed amount for a zone Neil's usual place of residence was in Zone A for 190 days and in Zone B for 40 days. **Table 3** shows that the fixed amount for Zone A is higher than the Zone B amount. Neil uses the Zone A amount because this will give him the greater benefit. He ignores the time that his usual place of residence was in Zone B. End of example ### Category 1 Your usual place of residence was only in one zone or you served only in specified overseas localities for at least 183 days. #### Step 1 Complete **worksheet 5** to work out your tax offset for one zone or location. | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Your fixed amount from [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3). | $ | | b | Your base amount from [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **g**. | $ | | c | Multiply row **b** by the percentage figure from [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3). | $ | | d | Add rows **a** and **c**
If you're claiming an **overseas forces tax offset**, the amount you can claim is row **d**. Go to step 2.
If you're claiming a zone tax offset, read on. | $ | | e | Any remote area allowance you received. | $ | | f | Subtract row **e** from row **d** and write the answer at row **f** | $ | Worksheet 5: Zone calculation, one zone or location If the amount at row **f** is more than zero (0), the amount is your **zone tax offset**. Go to step 2. #### Step 2 Write your zone or overseas forces tax offset amount at question **T4** – label **R** in your supplementary tax return. Don't show cents. See, [Where to go next](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Wheretogonext29). ### Category 2 Your usual place of residence was in more than one zone, or you either: - served in a specified overseas locality for less than 183 days - served in a specified overseas locality and you served in one or more zones for a total of at least 183 days. You claim for the number of days in each eligible place divided by 183, to a maximum of 183 days for a year. Start with your zone that has the highest fixed amount in [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3). This will give you the greatest benefit. #### Example: number of days in an eligible place Sharon's usual place of residence was in Zone A for 100 days and 120 days in Zone B. Sharon claims 100 ÷ 183 days for Zone A and 83 ÷ 183 days for Zone B. End of example #### Example: served in a specified overseas locality Sharon served 100 days in a specified overseas locality. Sharon claims 100 ÷ 183 days. End of example #### Example: overseas locality as a member of the defence forces and a zone Sharon served 100 days in an overseas locality as a member of the defence forces and served a further 83 days or more in a zone. Sharon claims the full overseas forces tax offset. End of example #### Example: served in an overseas locality and your usual place of residence Sharon served 100 days in an overseas locality and their usual place of residence was in a special area for 185 days. As the special area in [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3) shows the highest fixed amount and Sharon uses the maximum 183 days for this, Sharon claims the full special area amount and ignores the 100 days in an overseas locality. End of example #### Step 1 To work out your claim for each zone, special area or overseas locality, use [worksheet 6](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet6). For help applying the amounts in worksheet 6, see the [examples](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Examples). | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Your fixed amount from [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3). | $ | | b | Your base amount from [worksheet 4](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet4) – row **g**. | $ | | c | Multiply row **b** by the percentage figure from [table 3](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Table3). | $ | | d | Add row **a** and row **c**. | $ | | e | Number of days your usual place of residence was in a zone or special area or you served in an overseas locality, to a maximum of 183 days (see [examples](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Examples)). | days | | f | Multiply row **d** by row **e** | $ | | g | Divide row **f** by 183. This is the amount you can claim. | $ | Worksheet 6: Zone calculation, more than one zone or location #### Step 2 Once you work out the amount you can claim for each place, add up all the amounts and then use [worksheet 7](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet7) to work out your total tax offset. | Row | Calculation | Amount | | --- | --- | --- | | a | Total of the amounts you work out for each zone from [worksheet 6](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t4-zone-or-overseas-forces-2026#Worksheet6) – row **g**.
If you're claiming an **overseas forces tax offset**, the amount you can claim is row **a**. Go to step 3.
If you're claiming a zone tax offset, read on. | $ | | b | Any remote area allowance you received. | $ | | c | Subtract row **b** from row **a**. This is the amount you can claim. | $ | Worksheet 7: Total tax offset calculation If the amount at row **c**, is more than zero (0), the amount is the total of your **zone tax offset**. Go to step 3. #### Step 3 Write your zone or overseas forces total tax offset amount at question **T4** – label **R**. Don't show cents. ## Where to go next - Go to question [T5 Invalid and invalid carer 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t5-invalid-and-invalid-carer-2026). - Return to main menu [Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions). - Go back to question [T3 Superannuation contributions on behalf of your spouse 2026](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-supplementary-tax-return-2026-instructions/tax-offset-questions-t3-t9-supplementary-tax-return-2026/t3-super-contributions-on-behalf-of-your-spouse-2026).
